rule: docs/TREE_PLAN.md: one yard tree for every two or three houses, in back yards and at lot corners, never against a fence or a wall (zone 813 -> about 400)
written: by hand, 19 Nov 2026 (cloud session, the city-wide superchecker run from the bottom of the list). The quadrant's twenty-six builder trees go (a row of torrey pines, queen palms and corals every 6-8 m along the back fences, a palm 3 m from a house front, a few in the yards); six come back on their own spots, about one for every two or three houses: by the picnic table, the adirondack chairs, the beach umbrella, the open lot corner, and one on the old back fence row.

trees.why: the shared back lawn with the picnic table and the shade sail: a magnolia beside them
the same lawn 23 m east, 13 m from any wall: the lawn's second tree
the big open lot corner, 35 m from the walls: one norfolk pine, a landmark seen from the street
the back yard with the two white adirondack chairs: shade for them
the south-west back yard by the closed beach umbrella, 5.7 m from the house
the west end of the north back fence row, 5.3 m from the house: the row's one tree (it had one every 6 m)
